subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What native skill trust model should OpenClaw adopt for signed, unsigned, and unverifiable `SKILL.md` content?
rationale: The remaining work sets a security boundary and could intentionally block or degrade existing installed skills, so automation cannot choose the trust root, signature format, revocation behavior, or compatibility policy alone.

options.title: Staged signed-skill enforcement
options.body: Define a signed trust envelope and loader-time verification now, start unsigned skills in an explicit warning/degraded mode, and reserve strict blocking for a documented policy milestone.

options.title: Advisory verification only
options.body: Keep install and `skills verify` metadata informational, which preserves compatibility but leaves runtime prompt loading without an enforceable trust boundary.

options.title: Strict signed-only loading
options.body: Require valid signatures before loading ClawHub skills, which gives the clearest boundary but risks breaking existing users without a migration window.

recommendation.title: Staged signed-skill enforcement
recommendation.body: Define a signed trust envelope and loader-time verification now, start unsigned skills in an explicit warning/degraded mode, and reserve strict blocking for a documented policy milestone.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior review and discussion route this as canonical product/security trust-boundary work rather than a narrow implementation patch.
